desc:
The string words lists distinct non-empty lowercase words separated by single commas.

Count the ordered pairs of different list positions (i, j), i != j, for which the concatenation words[i] + words[j] is a palindrome. The pairs (i, j) and (j, i) are counted separately when both qualify.

words = "abcd,dcba,lls,s,sssll"  -> 4
  abcd+dcba = "abcddcba", dcba+abcd = "dcbaabcd", s+lls = "slls", lls+sssll = "llssssll"
words = "bat,tab,cat"            -> 2   (bat+tab and tab+bat)
words = "a,b,c"                  -> 0
constraints: All words are distinct and consist of lowercase English letters
hints: Checking all n² ordered pairs and testing each concatenation costs O(n² · L), about 12 million character steps for n = 1,000. Think about how a palindrome concatenation is structured.
If a + b is a palindrome and a is at least as long as b, then a splits into P + Q where Q is itself a palindrome and P is the reverse of b.

So for every word and every split point, test whether one part is a palindrome and look up the reverse of the other part in a hash map of all words. Handle the case where the whole word is the 'other part' carefully so that no pair is counted twice and no word is paired with itself.
editorial: Store every word in a dictionary. Consider a pair (a, b) with a + b a palindrome. Because the concatenation reads the same backwards, the shorter word must be the reverse of the matching end of the longer word, and what remains in the middle must be a palindrome. If b is the longer (or equal) word, b = P + Q with P a palindrome and a = reverse(Q). If a is strictly longer, a = P + Q with Q a palindrome and b = reverse(P).

So, for each word w and each split w = left + right (with left possibly empty, or right possibly empty): if left is a palindrome, the word reverse(right) placed before w gives a pair (reverse(right), w); if right is a palindrome and non-empty, the word reverse(left) placed after w gives a pair (w, reverse(left)). Requiring right to be non-empty in the second case is what prevents double counting equal-length pairs, which the first case finds from the other word. Skip the match when it is w itself (a palindromic word is its own reverse). Because every ordered pair is generated exactly once, the counts add up directly. Cost: O(n · L²) for palindrome tests and dictionary look-ups, about 150,000 character steps.
